content.text:
**Observations**

- *Which pixels were ever used.* A large set of W1 rows still look like untouched initialisation (all 16 values random, |w| ≲ 0.035): all of image row 0 (except a faint touch at cols 12–15), the first ~1–2 columns of the upper rows, and the two bottom corners (row 26 cols 0–3 and 23–27, row 27 cols 0–9 and 24–27). Everything else — from row 1 down to row 27, from col ~1 out to col 27 — carries trained weights. So the training images have content reaching row 1, row 27, col 26/27, i.e. the objects fill essentially the whole 28×28 canvas with only a ~1‑pixel margin at the top. That is not the 4‑pixel empty border of MNIST‑style digits.
- *Where the weights are largest.* The biggest magnitudes (0.2–0.4) are not in the centre but on the **periphery / silhouette**:
  - a top band, rows 1–3, strong at cols 2–10 and 17–25 but weak at the centre cols 11–16 (a "shoulders" pattern, widening from cols 4–23 at row 1 to 2–25 at rows 2–3);
  - a vertical line of very large, same‑sign weights at col ≈26 (plus 25/27) running from about row 6 to row 22, entering at col 23 (row 3) → 24 → 25 → 26 and coming back to col 23–24 at row 23 — i.e. the right‑hand extent of a wide object;
  - a bottom‑left corner patch, rows 24–26, cols 3–8 (e.g. unit 5: 0.18–0.34), plus the bottom rows 26–27 at cols 10–23;
  - a narrow central vertical strip, cols 12–15, rows 11–18, where unit 4 is strongly positive (0.25–0.36) and unit 5 strongly negative (−0.15 to −0.25) — a "is the centre lit or is there a gap" detector.
- *Hidden units.* Unit 5 = bottom‑left corner + bottom row on, centre strip off; its W2 row sends it to class 9 (1.70), 0 (0.84), 5 (0.60), 7 (0.51) and against 4 (−1.24), 8 (−0.82), 2, 6, 1. Unit 4 = centre strip + right edge on, top rows off → class 8 (1.21), 5, 3, 2 and against 0 (−1.47), 4 (−1.16), 7 (−1.09). Units 0/1/3/13 are dominated by the top shoulder band (unit 1 positive, 0/3/13 negative); unit 13 also has the right‑edge line and bottom centre negative, feeding classes 8, 1, 9. Many units carry the right‑edge line with a fixed sign pattern (+ for units 2,3,4,6,7,10,11,12; − for 0,5,8,9,13,14,15).
- *Output layer.* W2 entries are O(1) (up to ±1.7), b2 mild (class 5 highest +0.41, class 0 lowest −0.37). Reading signs through the shared features: the bottom‑left‑corner feature pushes classes 9 and 7 strongly up and 1, 0 down; the top‑shoulder feature pushes 0 and 6 up and 1, 7, 9 down. Classes 5/7/9 behave like one family (bottom of frame), 0/2/6 like another (top band), 1 and 8 are singled out by the centre‑strip/right‑edge units.

**Reasoning**

The content footprint (rows 1–27, cols ~1–27, nearly empty row 0) rules out MNIST and EMNIST, whose characters sit in a 20×20 box with an empty 4‑px (EMNIST ~2‑px) border — pixel (1,10) or (27,15) would never be lit and the weights there would still be at initialisation. notMNIST glyphs fill the entire frame including row 0 and show stroke‑like interior structure, not what we see. KMNIST/handwritten characters would have their discriminative weights in the interior as stroke templates, not a consistent‑sign vertical line hugging the right edge for 17 rows.

What we do see is the signature of **object silhouettes scaled to fill the canvas (longest side ≈ 28 px, ~1 px margin)**: the discriminative information is *how far* the object extends — to the top shoulders, to the right edge, to the bottom‑left corner — plus whether the exact centre is filled or has a vertical gap. That is exactly Fashion‑MNIST: shoes (sandal/sneaker/ankle boot) are low, wide shapes with the sole along the bottom and the toe in the bottom‑left corner (classes 9, 7 light up from that patch); tops (T‑shirt, pullover, coat, shirt) have shoulders in rows 1–3 and sleeves reaching col 26; trousers are tall and narrow with a dark gap at cols 12–15 (the unit‑4/5 centre strip); bags are wide with a short height (unit 4: right edge + centre on, top rows off → class 8). The class groupings implied by W2 (5/7/9 footwear, 0/2/6 tops, 1 trousers, 8 bag) match the Fashion‑MNIST label order.

**Dataset**

Fashion‑MNIST (Zalando clothing‑article thumbnails, 28×28 grayscale, 10 classes).

**Classes**

0 T‑shirt/top, 1 Trouser, 2 Pullover, 3 Dress, 4 Coat, 5 Sandal, 6 Shirt, 7 Sneaker, 8 Bag, 9 Ankle boot.

**Confidence**

78%
